# awscc_networkflowmonitor_monitor (Resource)

Creates a monitor for specific network flows between local and remote resources to monitor network performance for workloads.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `local_resources` (Attributes List) The local resources to monitor. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--local_resources))
- `monitor_name` (String) The name of the monitor.

### Optional

- `remote_resources` (Attributes List) The remote resources to monitor. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--remote_resources))
- `scope_arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the scope for the monitor.
- `tags` (Attributes List) The tags for the monitor. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tags))

### Read-Only

- `arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the monitor.
- `created_at` (String) The date and time when the monitor was created.
- `id` (String) Uniquely identifies the resource.
- `modified_at` (String) The date and time when the monitor was last modified.
- `monitor_status` (String) The status of the monitor.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = awscc_networkflowmonitor_monitor.example
  identity = {
    arn = "arn"
  }
}
```

#### Optional

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:
